frequency_question: How often do structural frictions (industry pushback, technical integration hurdles, compliance delays) successfully prevent or delay the implementation of contested financial mandates on the scheduled date?
membership_rule: Includes major government or central bank mandated merchant fee changes, interoperability deadlines, or digital payment compliance requirements in major emerging economies (e.g., India, Brazil, Indonesia) since 2015. Excludes advisory guidelines without enforcement mechanisms.

cases.name: RBI tokenization mandate initial deadline extension
RBI auto-debit processing (e-mandate) additional factor of authentication enforcement
NPCI 30% volume cap on third-party UPI apps deadline extension
SEBI T+1 stock settlement cycle implementation
RBI payment aggregator licensing compliance deadline extension
Reserve Bank of India card storage ban enforcement
GST e-invoicing mandatory rollout for mid-tier businesses phase
UPI Lite automatic replenishment feature rollout

coverage_note: 8 named major contested payment/fintech regulatory deadlines in India; 3 resulted in delays/deferrals due to structural friction.
known_gaps: Focuses primarily on Indian regulatory environment due to high relevance, though structural friction dynamics are broadly similar across large emerging digital economies.
validity_reason: Regulatory enforcement posture and industry lobbying capacity evolve slowly over multi-year technology policy cycles.
